text:
marta: Quick triage: after yesterday's kernel-roll we see host-side CPU tail on small-chat workload. Putting notes here.

marta: baseline host-parse p95: 210ms, canary p95: 330ms. Throughput -3% on chat-short QPS.

sam: any flame graphs?

marta: Yes, attaching summary: top diffs from perf sample: parse_tokenize +22pts, memcpy +11pts, grpc_frame_decode +4pts. kv_cache_lookup slightly down (5% -> 4%).

preethi: Sounds like extra work before batching. What changed in selector?

marta: Selector now picks "vec_fast" kernel for seq_len <= 48 and tries to flatten fragments into a contiguous buffer before passing to GPU. We introduced an ephemeral copy + new malloc path.

theo: That copy also allocs per-request, right? That explains mem alloc rate bump in CI.

infra-bot: CI quick metrics for this canary:
- host-parse CPU: +15%
- allocs/sec: +30%
- small-chat p95: +57%
- kvcache hit-rate: -0.4%

sam: Two orthogonal issues: extra memcpy/allocs and possible kvcache key variance if normalization occurs. We should avoid per-request heap allocs.

preethi: Proposal: 1) revert canary selector (temporary) 2) implement sticky buffer pool per-thread to reuse linearization buffer (no allocs) 3) make kernel fragment-aware so it can operate on scatter/segments without copying.

marta: I also wonder if we can change batching heuristics: for HTTP/gRPC ingress, many small fragments come from clients. If we delay kernel selection until after batching we might amortize a single linearization cost across N requests in a batch.

theo: Good point. If we postpone kernel_choice until post-merge step we can decide based on resulting contiguous batch buffer. That avoids copying each request twice.

sam: Microbench ideas: a) small-chat QPS replay with sticky pool vs baseline b) post-batch-linearize flow c) fragment-aware kernel microkernel latency. We'll measure p50/p95 and allocs.

preethi: I'll add telemetry tags: kernel_choice, linearize_mode={none,sticky,persistent}, sticky_reuse_ratio, preparse_copy=true/false, batch_merged=true/false. That should make the comparison obvious in perf dashboards.

marta: Also add kvcache normalization tag: kvcache_key_source={orig,normalized,linearized}. If keys change we need to normalize deterministically.

theo: Short-term patch: implement sticky buffer pool (per-worker char[] reused) and gate heap alloc behind pool miss. If pool size large enough miss-rate should be near zero.

sam: For long-term, prefer making the kernel accept iovecs. But that's a non-trivial kernel rewrite. Submit a design doc for kernel-segmented-io acceptance.

infra-bot: Rollback PR deployed to canary at 08:12; canary running baseline selector. Monitoring for 20m.

marta: Post-rollback quick numbers (08:35): memcpy sample portion back to 2%, allocs/sec back down 95%, host-parse p95 at 218ms. Looks like revert fixed immediate regression.

preethi: Filing follow-ups: RTX-4910 sticky-buffer pool implementation, RTX-4911 postpone-selector-to-post-batch, and RTX-4912 design doc for kernel iovec support.

sam: Someone pick up sticky-pool and the microbench; I'll take kernel design doc.

marta: I'll own the microbench and telemetry dashboards. Attaching short replay script and flame screenshot to RTX-4910.

preethi: Thanks all. Next steps: land sticky pool experiment behind feature flag, run canary with feature flag on 10% to validate no kvcache regressions, then iterate.

theo: Also track grpc framing overhead: if we can coalesce small stream writes at ingress we reduce per-request syscall cost. I'll prototype a small coalescer in ingress path.

marta: Nice. Keep updates in this thread.

preethi: I'll post perf diffs once sticky-pool PR is up.

sam: Great work, quick detection + rollback.
